source.title: Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards

teaching.hint: After any exact-k sequence of end picks, what shape do the untouched cards have?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: All selected cards form a prefix plus a suffix; their complement is one contiguous block of length n−k.
solution_outline.approach: Compute the total points and subtract the minimum sum among all length-(n−k) contiguous blocks.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: A fixed-length block represents exactly the cards left untouched by one valid split of k picks between the two ends.
solution_outline.correctness: Every valid selection maps to a unique untouched block, and every such block can be created by taking its outside prefix and suffix. Maximizing selected score is therefore minimizing untouched score.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
solution_outline.pitfall: Greedily taking the larger visible end can miss a valuable card just behind a smaller one.

common_wrong_turns: Choose the larger current end at every move
source_fidelity_notes: Kept exact-k and k=n cases; removed narrative card example.
